free_tier.stated: The free Basic tier is 5 GB of Data Store storage, 200 compute units per year and 1 concurrent job, where the page states "1 Compute Unit equals 1 Core Hour on a CPU". Paid individual tiers are Regular at USD 200 per year for 50 GB, 1,000 compute units and 2 concurrent jobs, and Pro at USD 400 per year for 4 TB, 25,000 compute units and 4 concurrent jobs, with GPU access by request on the two paid tiers only.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: CyVerse is the funding parent of the Galaxy Main hardware allocation, so the two accounts sit on overlapping machines; the useful composition is the paid Pro tier, where USD 400 a year buys 25,000 core-hours and 4 TB on the same infrastructure that hosts Galaxy, which is a batch analysis machine with a shell rather than Galaxy wrappers.

limits.value: 5 GB of storage and 200 core-hours a year on the free tier, enforced since 1 March 2025, and the user portal states that data above quota is deleted and is not recoverable.

"1 Compute Unit equals 1 Core Hour on a CPU", quoted

"Starting March 1, 2025, we will begin to enforce data storage quotas and limits on all Basic (free) and paid subscription accounts"; "data exceeding your storage quota will be removed. Deleted data are not recoverable", quoted
"All domestic and international CyVerse account holders receive a default allocation of 5GB of storage at no cost", quoted

notes: The free tier is small enough that recording it as capacity would mislead: 200 core-hours a year is one afternoon of a single core. Its value is the paid tier as a price floor, and the enforcement history as a reliability fact. It is not the cheapest cost per core-hour in the file: the DesignSafe record carries a TACC purchase rate near USD 0.008 to USD 0.01 per core-hour, but that is a quote-based purchase from a national laboratory rather than a published annual plan. CyVerse also removes accounts for inactivity, announced on its own 404 page, which is a fact a reader storing data there needs. The corpus holds no CyVerse record.
